beliefs: On x>=0, f(x) = 106.06 + 111.43*x is accurate to ~0.1% across 0.1 to 127 [E1, E2, E3]
On x<=-2, f(x) = 26.07*|x| - 25.4 is accurate to ~0.1% across |x| from 2 to 128 [E5, E6, E3, E4]

The negative branch dips below the linear law near |x|=1: f(-1)=6.85, f(-1.1)=6.44, f(-1.2)=7.47, f(-1.4)=11.24, f(-1.6)=16.27, f(-1.8)=21.48, f(-1.9)=24.09, f(-2)=26.70 — a smooth trough bottoming near |x|=1.05 [E7, E8, E4]
For |x| between 0 and 1, f rises steeply from ~6.85 at |x|=1 to ~106 at x=0, roughly linear: f(-0.5)=50.34, f(-0.3)=72.62, f(-0.1)=94.91, f(-0.02)=103.82 [E8, E4, E2]
f(0)≈106 is a spike; both branches approach ~106 at x=0 [E1, E3]
notes: Replaced the wrong quadratic near-zero model with a piecewise fit: linear rise from ~106 at x=0 down to ~6.85 at |x|=1, then a smooth trough up to the linear law at |x|=2. The dip minimum is near |x|=1.05.
